tool.help:
**Proteins Mosaic Q**
Calculates the Mosaic Q and Q_alt structural descriptors for a protein from the Protein Data Bank and renders an interactive 3D visualisation coloured by amino acid chemical family.
-----
**Input**
Either a 4-character PDB ID (e.g. ``1CRN``, ``4HHB``, ``1TIM``) fetched automatically from the RCSB Protein Data Bank, or a PDB file already present in the Galaxy history (useful for artificial or modified structures not available in the PDB).
-----
**Output**
An HTML page showing:
- Interactive 3D structure coloured by chemical family (spacefill/VDW representation) - Q and Q_alt descriptor values - Colour legend
-----
**Chemical family colouring**
+-----------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Colour | Residues | +=================+==============================================+ | White | Hydrophobic: Ala, Val, Ile, Leu, Met, | | | Phe, Tyr, Trp | +-----------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Green | Polar: Ser, Thr, Asn, Gln | +-----------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Orange | Acidic: Asp, Glu | +-----------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Blue | Basic: Arg, His, Lys | +-----------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Cyan | Special: Cys, Sec, Gly, Pro | +-----------------+----------------------------------------------+
-----
**The Mosaic Q descriptor**
Big-data analysis of the >160,000 protein structures in the Protein Data Bank points to an apparently conserved structural trait: the presence of particular amino acid 3D clustering pattern, where along with the existence of the hydrophobic core, amino acids tend to cluster in space according to their chemical family in groups of approximately 8 residues, forming a characteristic mosaic-like pattern (**Mosaic Q**).
This clustering is captured by the **Q descriptor**, defined as a sum of inverse inter-residue distances within each chemical family. Q follows a precise empirical equation (R² = 0.979) that depends only on the total number of residues. **Q_alt** extends this to include special residues (Cys, Sec, Gly, Pro).
-----
**How to participate**
Your observation contributes to a growing community-based repository of evidence. After running the tool:
1. Inspect the rendered structure — do amino acids of the same chemical type cluster together in groups of approximately the same size and shape? 2. Save a screenshot. 3. Email your image to protmsq@qmosaic.org with the PDB ID and your name. Your image will appear in the repository and you will receive a certificate of contribution.
More information at https://proteins-mosaic-q.org
- Preprint: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/500025v1.full - Updated manuscript: https://github.com/UPO-Sevilla-Fco-Javier-Lobo-Cabrera/clustering_trait_proteins/blob/main/Manuscript_and_Supplementary_Materials_v4.pdf
